chapter: After the Paradise: club dates and Virginia
title: Never taking non-music jobs; his wife's urging and other musicians' day jobs
summary: He never worked outside music; his wife urged the Post Office, and he mentions musicians who became bank guards, union delegates and salesmen.

story.theme_name: Making a living: hard times, day jobs and scarce work
story.community_name: Day jobs: musicians working outside music

blocks.x: Something occurs to me here that
I was going to ask way back. Other ways of getting by, financially: Did you ever take jobs other than jobs as a musician?

No, I never did. No, I never did that because...you know...I know some guys that did but, you know, it seems to take away. I don't know, if you have to do it, you have to do it. But it seemed to take away from me and I didn't think I had the temperament for that type of thing. But I guess if things had really got real, real, real bad I would have done that too, you know. 'Cause I know other guys that did, there was a lot of guys that became delegates to the union and some guys, like Hilton Jefferson, he became a bank guard and Jonah Jones, before he got his break, he was thinkin' about becomin' a bank guard, you know. And guys were doin' different things, you know. A lot of the things they were doin' I don't even know nuthin' about because...and then, there was really no stigma to it, but it was a little sad, you know. So you try to hang on as long as you can, you
know, before you have to make a decision like that, you know what I mean.
Did it ever seem to you at some point that...
Oh yeah, many times. (laughter) Yeah, there's been some rough weeks there.
So where was your wife in this, in terms of the...
Well she was workin' all the time, yeah.
Would she urge you at some points that you should take...
Yeah, she told me to go in the Post Office and get somethin' steady, you know.
I guess Charlie Mingus worked in
the Post Office at one time.

Oh, I know, J.J. Johnson was...I think he's still in the Post Office out on the coast. Sure. I know Roy Haynes became a whiskey salesman. You know, you try to think about different things. Try to survive, that's the whole thing. You see what I mean. Tryin' to make it, see. But I didn't do anything, say "I'm gonna try to make it some kinda way." Of course I was learning all the time, you know, about all facets of the business, you know what I mean. So all these things that you learn, you know, you put 'em in the bank and one day it will all come out, you see. But the lessons were hard. Yeah. (laughter) Yeah, they were hard Dale.
